findings.explanation: All premises of the HOL4 theorem are dropped: q has_type Bool, term_ok (sigof thy) q, the semantic implication from p1 and p2 to q over all structures, and (thy,h1) |= p1, (thy,h2) |= p2. The Lean statement says that in any set theory every term q is entailed by every theory under any hypotheses, and p1 and p2 are unused. It is strictly stronger and false. Example: for q = Var x (Tyvar a), entails0 requires has_type q BoolTy, which fails. So the statement together with is_set_theory mem yields False, while the HOL4 theorem is a true conditional rule.
findings.repair:
theorem binary_inference_rule [Nonempty U] (mem : U → U → Prop) :
    is_set_theory mem →
      ∀ (thy : thy) (h1 h2 : List term) (p1 p2 q : term),
        has_type q BoolTy ∧ term_ok (sigof thy) q ∧
        (∀ (i : interpretation U) (v : valuation U),
          is_structure0 mem (sigof thy) i v ∧
          termsem0 mem (thy_tmsof thy) i v p1 = true_ mem ∧
          termsem0 mem (thy_tmsof thy) i v p2 = true_ mem →
          termsem0 mem (thy_tmsof thy) i v q = true_ mem) ∧
        entails0 mem (thy, h1) p1 ∧ entails0 mem (thy, h2) p2 →
        entails0 mem (thy, term_union h1 h2) q := by sorry
findings.lean_check:
import CandleLean.HolSoundness

universe u

namespace Candle

open HOL Classical

theorem binary_inference_rule_refuted {U : Type u} [Nonempty U] (mem : U → U → Prop)
    (hs : is_set_theory mem) (H : type_of% (@binary_inference_rule U _ mem)) : False := by
  have h := H hs ((FEMPTY, FEMPTY), EMPTY) [] [] (Var (mls "x") (Tyvar (mls "a")))
    (Var (mls "x") (Tyvar (mls "a"))) (Var (mls "x") (Tyvar (mls "a")))
  unfold entails0 at h
  obtain ⟨_, _, h2, _⟩ := h
  simp only [EVERY] at h2
  have h3 : has_type (Var (mls "x") (Tyvar (mls "a"))) BoolTy := h2.1
  cases h3

end Candle
